        ### Question
        A 54-year-old man with hypertension and congenital blindness comes to the physician because he is unable to recognize objects by touch with his right hand. The symptoms started about 2 hours ago. When given a house key, he can feel the object in his right hand but is not able to identify what it is. This patient's condition is most likely caused by a lesion in which of the following locations?

        ### Options
        opa. Ipsilateral inferior frontal gyrus
opb. Ipsilateral superior temporal gyrus
opc. Contralateral superior parietal lobule
opd. Contralateral precentral gyrus
ope. Ipsilateral cingulate gyrus

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Impaired object recognition by touch in the right hand -> Lesion affecting somatosensory processing in the brain -> Likely located in the contralateral superior parietal lobule -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: Inability to identify objects by touch in the right hand -> Disruption in tactile perception pathways -> Lesion possibly in the contralateral superior parietal lobule -> 80%

### Retrieved Evidence Paths (broad but correct):
(Structure of right hand)-PART_OF->(Nerve)-PART_OF->(Brain)
